name: Graph state stabiliser (fixpoint property)
aliases: X on a vertex, Z on its neighbours
summary: Applying X to a vertex of a graph state and Z to all its neighbours leaves the graph state unchanged.
description:
For every vertex $u$ of a graph $G$, the Pauli operator $X_u \prod_{v\in N(u)} Z_v$ stabilises the graph state $|G\rangle$. Graphically: the X-spider with phase π on the output of $u$ is copied through the Z-spider $u$, turns into Z-spiders with phase π after passing the Hadamard edges, and these fuse with the π phases on the neighbours, which cancel.

These $|V(G)|$ operators generate the stabiliser group of the graph state. The property is also what one gets by applying [local complementation of graph states](../graph-state-local-complementation/) twice at the same vertex, since $(G\star u)\star u = G$.
parameter_notes: n is the number of neighbours of u (shown for n = 3). The neighbours may be connected to further vertices, which are left unchanged.
